# Thai Token Tax · ภาษีภาษา

**The same Thai text takes 2.14× the tokens on Claude as on GPT, and 2.59× as on Gemini.**
APIs bill per token, so the bill follows. At the same list price ($4 in / $20 out per
million tokens), an example workload (LINE OA customer chatbot, 10,000 conversations a month) costs 29,121 baht on Claude Opus 5.5 and
13,635 baht on GPT-5.6 Sol.

| Tokenizer (models that share it) | Tokens per 1,000 Thai characters |  |
|---|---:|---|
| Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5, Fable 5.2 | 889.5 | ███████████████████████ |
| GPT-5.x and GPT-6 | 416.5 | ███████████ |
| Gemini 3.x, Gemma 4, Typhoon 2.1 | 344.1 | █████████ |
| Gemini 4 Argon | 325.9 | ████████ |

This measures **cost, not answer quality**: a model that uses more tokens may still answer Thai better.
45 models (13 distinct tokenizers) on 1,012 parallel Thai–English sentences
(FLORES-200), measured 10 November 2026; official list prices as of 11 November 2026.

Reproduce it:

```
git clone https://github.com/neptunenakub/thai-token-tax thai-token-tax && cd thai-token-tax
pip install -e .
ttt all --out rerun
```

[ภาษาไทย](README.th.md) · [Method and limits](docs/methodology.md) · [Result files](results/) ·
web page with a cost calculator: <https://neptunenakub.github.io/thai-token-tax/>

---

## Reproducing

- Needs Python 3.11 or newer (use a virtual environment) and no API key. 
- `ttt all` downloads FLORES-200 (about 26 MB) and the tokenizer files, counts every sentence with
  every local tokenizer, recounts in a second independent way, and writes `rerun/summary_<date>.md`.
- Those rows must equal the rows with source `open` in [`results/summary_2026-11-10_day2c.md`](results/summary_2026-11-10_day2c.md).
  The published per-sentence counts are in `results/counts_2026-11-10_open.csv`.
- Claude, GPT and Gemini are counted through their official token-counting endpoints. Without
  `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `GEMINI_API_KEY` those sources are reported as blocked and
  skipped; gated Hugging Face repositories need `HF_TOKEN`. A model that cannot be measured is listed as
  blocked with the real error. It is never replaced by an estimate.
- Result files are never overwritten: every run writes a new dated set, which is why the example writes
  to `rerun/`. `ttt prepare` (the first step of `ttt all`) also rewrites `data/source.json` and
  `data/normalization_log.json`; only their timestamps should change.
- `pytest` runs the tests (no network, no keys): `pip install -e ".[dev]"`, then `pytest -q`.

## What is measured, and what is not

Every model's own tokenizer counts the same content in Thai and in English. Two numbers come out, and
they answer different questions:

- **Tokens per 1,000 Thai characters** compares models with each other: the same Thai text, how many
  tokens. Multiplied by a price it gives the bill.
- **Thai ÷ English** (the "premium") compares the two languages inside one model, with a 95%
  bootstrap confidence interval. It cannot be compared across models, because each model spends a
  different number of tokens on English. Example: from Claude Haiku 4.5 to Claude Opus 5.5 the premium fell from
  3.870 to 2.676, yet Thai tokens per 1,000 characters barely moved
  (886.5 → 889.5) while English rose from 218.9 to
  317.6.

Baht costs are measured tokens × official list price × the Bank of Thailand rate, for example
workloads whose sizes are assumptions.

Not measured: answer quality, speed, reasoning or thinking tokens, prompt caching, batch discounts, and
any kind of text other than the FLORES-200 sentences (news and encyclopedia style).

| Nemotron-SEA-LION v4.8 | open models only | 521.8 | █████████████ | 210.9 | 2.365 (2.335–2.395) | 1 |
| Llama 3.1, Llama 3.3, Typhoon 2 (Llama 3.1) | open models only | 470.7 | ████████████ | 205.9 | 2.185 (2.159–2.211) | 4 |

| Gemma-SEA-LION v3 | open models only | 394.9 | ██████████ | 204.9 | 1.842 (1.817–1.867) | 1 |
| Gemini 3.x, Gemma 4, Typhoon 2.1 | API | 344.1 | █████████ | 205.5 | 1.600 (1.580–1.621) | 7 |
| Gemini 4 Argon | API | 325.9 | ████████ | 205.0 | 1.519 (1.500–1.538) | 1 |
| Typhoon 7B | open models only | 303.9 | ████████ | 227.5 | 1.276 (1.262–1.291) | 1 |

One row is one distinct tokenizer. Models in a row gave identical token counts on every sentence
(models measured on a sample: on every sampled sentence). The table of all 45 models is
[`results/summary_2026-11-10_day2c.md`](results/summary_2026-11-10_day2c.md).

Qwen3, Typhoon 2.5, OpenThaiGPT 1.5 / 1.6 / R1 give identical counts: 556.7 tokens per 1,000 Thai characters. The Thai
models in this group inherit the base model's tokenizer.

### Same list price, different bill

Example workload: LINE OA customer chatbot, 10,000 conversations a month.

| List price, $ per 1M tokens (in / out) | Model | Thai | Model | Thai | Ratio |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|---:|
| $4 / $20 | Claude Opus 5.5 | 29,121 baht | GPT-5.6 Sol | 13,635 baht | 2.14× |
| $0.10 / $0.50 | Claude Haiku 5.5 | 728 baht | GPT-6 Luna | 341 baht | 2.14× |

More tokens does not always mean a higher bill: Claude Haiku 5.5 costs 728 baht, less than
Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite at 1,017 baht, although it uses more Thai tokens (889.5 vs
344.1 per 1,000 characters). The price per token differs.

Open models have no per-token price of their own, so they have token counts only. The other
workloads are in [`results/costs_2026-11-11.md`](results/costs_2026-11-11.md); the web page has a calculator with
editable assumptions.

The workloads (assumptions, from `registry/scenarios.toml`; sizes in Thai characters):

| Scenario | Volume | Turns | System prompt, chars | Input per turn, chars | Output per turn, chars | History resent |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| LINE OA customer chatbot, 10,000 conversations a month | 10,000 | 6 | 2,000 | 60 | 250 | yes |
| Summarising 100 Thai documents | 100 | 1 | 500 | 20,000 | 1,500 | no |
| Writing 1,000 Thai content pieces | 1,000 | 1 | 800 | 300 | 3,000 | no |

## Limits

- This is token cost only. It says nothing about answer quality.
- Token rates were measured on FLORES-200 (news and encyclopedia style text). Chat messages or other kinds of text may tokenize differently.
- Output tokens are assumed to have the same tokens-per-character as input text of that language.
- Reasoning/thinking tokens, prompt caching, batch discounts, free tiers and long-context price tiers are not included. Standard list prices only.
- Claude token rates come from count_tokens, which Anthropic documents as an estimate.
- Open models have no per-token price of their own: only their token counts are reported.
- The English column is the same content in English: character counts are scaled by the measured English/Thai character ratio of FLORES-200.
- Scenario sizes (characters, turns, volumes) are assumptions written in registry/scenarios.toml, not measurements.
- FLORES contains some translations whose meaning does not match the source. The data was not edited.
- The check against real billing (90 paid requests to Claude; billed input tokens equalled
  `count_tokens` on every one) covered single-message requests only: no system prompt, no tools.
- Claude's request framing (8 / 7 tokens per request) is billed, but is not part of these numbers.
- Prices change. On 11 November 2026 Google's pricing page stated an end date for the current price of:

- Gemini 3.8 Flash: input "$0.75 through December 31, 2026. $1.50 starting January 1, 2027." output "$3.75 through December 31, 2026. $7.50 starting January 1, 2027."
- Gemini 4 Argon: input "$2.00 through November 30, 2026. $4.00 starting December 1, 2026." output "$10.00 through November 30, 2026. $20.00 starting December 1, 2026."
- Gemini 3.6 Flash: input "$0.75 through December 31, 2026. $1.50 starting January 1, 2027." output "$3.75 through December 31, 2026. $7.50 starting January 1, 2027."

The full list of weak points, and what would change the conclusions, is in
[`docs/methodology.md`](docs/methodology.md).

## Adding a model or a language

Both are registry changes, not new code.

- **Model:** add one `[[model]]` block to `registry/models.toml` (`id`, `family`, `counter`; `revision`
  pins a Hugging Face repository; `sample_of` checks an API model against a fully measured one on a fixed
  sample). Then `ttt count`, `ttt verify`, `ttt analyze`. For a price, add its row to
  `registry/pricing.toml` and run `ttt prices` and `ttt cost`. Then `ttt site` and `ttt docs`.
- **Language:** add one `[[target]]` block with a FLORES-200 code to `registry/languages.toml`, then
  `ttt prepare` and the steps above. `prepare`, `count`, `verify` and `analyze` take every language in
  the registry; only Thai has been run so far, and the cost tables, the site and this README present one
  target language.

## Repository layout

```
registry/              what is measured: models, languages, price sources, example workloads, display names
src/thai_token_tax/    the `ttt` command: prepare, count, verify, analyze, prices, cost, compare, site, docs
tests/                 pytest, no network
data/                  provenance and logs; the FLORES sentences are rebuilt locally, not committed
results/               dated raw counts, summaries, prices, costs; latest.json points at the newest set
site/                  one static page; reads site/data.json, written by `ttt site`
templates/             the sources of this README and docs/methodology.md, filled by `ttt docs`
docs/methodology.md    how it was measured, limits, what would change the conclusions
blog/                  articles (Thai, English) and post drafts, generated like this README
ARCHITECTURE.md        how the code is organised
LOG.md                 what was run each day, including the things that went wrong
```

No number in this README, the methodology or the site is typed by hand: they are generated from
`results/`, and tests fail if a document is out of date.

## Dates and sources

- Token counts: measured 10 November 2026 (UTC). Raw per-sentence counts: `counts_2026-11-10_open.csv`, `counts_2026-11-10_open-llama31.csv`, `counts_2026-11-10_open-llama33.csv`, `counts_2026-11-10_openai.csv`, `counts_2026-11-10_gemini.csv`, `counts_2026-11-10_anthropic.csv`.
- Prices: official pricing pages of Anthropic, OpenAI and Google, fetched 11 November 2026, saved with the
  page hashes in `results/prices_2026-11-11.json`.
- Exchange rate: 33.392 baht per US dollar, Bank of Thailand weighted-average interbank exchange rate, baht per US dollar, 10 November 2026
  (<https://www.bot.or.th/en/statistics/exchange-rate.html>).
- Data: FLORES-200 `devtest`, English and Thai, the original Meta release. FLORES+ 5.0 differs
  from it in 0 of these sentences after normalization.
